source: Khieu Borin, Than Soeurn, Preston T.R. and Sato K. 1996. The role of the sugar palm tree (Borassus flabellifer) in livestock based farming systems in Cambodia. In: Sustainable Livestock Production on Local Feed Resources, FAO Regional Office for Asia and the Pacific (RAP Publication), Bangkok.
text: For long-term, sustainable smallholder pig breeding adapted to Cambodia's native environment and local feed resources, indigenous breeds — Chrouk Domrey, Chrouk Hainam, and Chrouk Kandor — are recommended over imported breeds, valued for their prolificacy, behavior, and efficient use of local feed. A recognized constraint in Cambodia's pig sector is that most farmers raise only fattening pigs rather than breeding sows, keeping the system unbalanced and piglet prices relatively high compared to finished-pig prices; establishing local breeding using these adapted native breeds is proposed as part of the solution.
caveat: This source names the three indigenous breeds but does not describe their physical characteristics, weights, or performance data in detail — flagged for future sourcing if breed-identification content is needed.
